message_log.text: 🏋️ Evening Weight Training - Sept 6 Grade: 7/10 - solid, low-strain strength session that slotted in cleanly around your running load RECOVERY CONTEXT (athletedata, before the session) Readiness was strong going in: recovery score 80, readiness verdict "go_hard", HRV 53 (above your 60d baseline of 48), resting HR 47. SUMMARY 77-minute strength session, avg HR just 83bpm (max 117bpm) - textbook low cardiovascular strain for a lifting day, exactly what you want between run sessions. Suffer score of 8 confirms this was easy on the aerobic system, all the work happening elsewhere. GOOD PARTS • Avg HR 83bpm for 77 minutes is very controlled - no cardiovascular stacking on top of your running fatigue • Session ran slightly over the 60-min target (77.7 min) without dragging your ACWR anywhere near a red zone • Body battery climbed steadily through the session (61 to 96 range across the evening block), showing you weren't digging into a big reserve deficit WATCH FOR • TSB at -15.2 (start-of-day) plus ramp_rate 0.8 means you're still net fatigued from the running block - keep this session's load easy/moderate rather than pushing new PRs on lifts right now • No zero-full-rest-day flag in the last 14 days - worth actually taking one soon given the fatigued form status OVERTRAINING CHECK: Moderate Reconciling the numbers: acwr sits at a sweet-spot 0.91, monotony 1.03 (healthy variability, not flatlined), and load_flag index is 0 with no active drivers - none of the anomaly signals are firing. But TSB at -15.2 (start-of-day) and the fatigued/absorbing-training form status, combined with zero full rest days in the past 14, mean you're running a real fatigue deficit even though this particular strength session barely dented it (avg HR 83bpm, dailyLoad only 25.9). Verdict: manageable now, but the lack of a genuine rest day is the actual lever - schedule one full rest day in the next 3-4 days before the next hard running session rather than letting TSB drift lower.
